visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the projectile setup with axes, parabolic path, launch angle/vector components, and relevant motion equation, while Lesson 2 uses a generic/stylized trajectory with ambiguous zero labels and no correct representation of the 40 m/s at 30° setup or range calculation.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in checkpoint after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and remediation path, whereas Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, natural narration with well-spoken math and pacing cues, while Lesson 2 contains multiple garbled/unnatural phrases such as “1 9.8 every second,” “0 verts,” “X2,” and awkward repetition/grammar that would noticeably hurt audio quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed visual cues that mostly coincide with the narration’s references to vectors, decomposition, vertical/horizontal focus, equations, and range, whereas Lesson 2 has no beat or cue timing data at all, making its visual-narration synchronization unverifiable and effectively unsupported.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 more clearly and correctly walks through the actual numerical reasoning—components, flight time via vertical motion, then range—whereas Lesson 1 has a sound conceptual structure but leaves key calculations like vertical component, time of flight, and numeric substitution mostly implicit in visuals and slightly overstates the range formula as generally valid for any projectile/angle.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a much more polished, visually engaging, and legible presentation with large clean graphics and balanced composition, whereas Lesson 1’s mid-lesson layout is off-center with tiny hard-to-read labels, excessive empty space, and a cluttered/faint UI-like split layout.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner after weighting the six dimension judgments. Four agents strongly favored Lesson 1, with very high confidence in visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, and synchronization. These strengths indicate that Lesson 1 better represents the projectile setup, includes functioning learner interaction, has clearer narration, and provides usable timing between visuals and audio. Lesson 2 was favored for concept accuracy and polish, including clearer numerical walkthrough and stronger visual presentation, but those two advantages do not outweigh Lesson 1's broader and higher-confidence wins across the other dimensions.
